title: Contractible incoming commas imply a left-anodyne monomorphism
statement: Use small simplicial sets, standard horns, quasicategories, weak homotopy equivalences and weak contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. Let $K,L$ be small quasicategories and $j:K\hookrightarrow L$ a degreewise injective simplicial map. For a vertex $l\in L$, define $L_{/l}$ in degree $a$ by maps $\Delta^a\star\Delta^0\to L$ with final vertex $l$, and let $K\times_L L_{/l}$ use the source projection $L_{/l}\to L$. Suppose every such comma quasicategory $K\times_L L_{/l}$ is weakly contractible, meaning its map to a point is a weak homotopy equivalence. Then $j$ is left anodyne: it belongs to the smallest class containing isomorphisms and all horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$ and $0\leq i<m$, and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. The image of $j$ need not be a full simplicial subset of $L$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.3.1 (cofinality detected by comma categories), printed p.236, followed by Proposition 4.1.1.3(4) (a cofinal inclusion is right anodyne), printed pp.223-224, both applied to opposite simplicial sets. Independently read in the retained HTT.pdf text. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion.
